positioning.text: UPMC describes itself as a Pittsburgh-headquartered health care provider and insurer and a global leader in research, treatments and clinical care. Its facts page lists more than 40 hospitals, 800 outpatient sites, 100,000 employees and more than four million insurance members. Its brand line is 'Life Changing Medicine'.
positioning.quote: Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, UPMC is a world-renowned health care provider and insurer.

facts.text: UPMC HealthBeat is described by UPMC as its blog for health and wellness information; its editorial policy says a team of writers produces the content and each article is reviewed by a medical expert in the topic.

facts.text: The HealthBeat home page offers an email newsletter sign-up ('Never Miss a Beat') and a sign-up for health tips by text message, and organizes articles under Living & Wellness, Health Topics A-Z and UPMC Stories.

facts.text: UPMC's podcasts page lists five shows: The UPMC Tele-Town Hall Podcast, UPMC HealthBeat Podcast, Psychiatry Advances (for mental health professionals), That's Pediatrics (UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh) and Healthier You (UPMC experts in Central Pennsylvania).

evidence.quote: Our guests discuss health and wellness, chronic disease, medical advancements — and much more.

facts.text: The Apple Podcasts listing for the UPMC HealthBeat Podcast, as shown on 2026-11-10, gave 85 episodes, a semimonthly schedule, a latest episode dated 06/23/2024 ('Help with Your Headaches') and a rating of 4.5 out of 5 from 2 ratings.

facts.text: MyUPMC is UPMC's patient portal, 'powered by MyChart', where patients can book appointments and virtual visits, see test results and manage bills; a MyUPMC app is offered on the Apple App Store and Google Play.

evidence.title: MyUPMC Patient Portal
evidence.quote: MyUPMC patient portal, powered by MyChart, offers secure access to your health information.

evidence.title: UPMC Mobile Apps for Android and iOS Devices

facts.text: UPMC Enterprises reported on June 29, 2020 that MyUPMC video visits rose from an average of 20 to 30 per day before the pandemic to 4,000 to 5,000 a day, with a 35% increase in active users in March 2020 compared with March 2019.

evidence.title: MyUPMC experiences major jump in video visits as patients move to online care
evidence.quote: the daily average has shot up to 4,000 to 5,000 a day.

facts.text: UPMC's brand line is 'Life Changing Medicine'. Becker's reported on October 21, 2010 that the tagline was introduced with a $16 million advertising campaign of newspaper and magazine ads, TV ads and a modified logo; a current 'Life Changing Is' campaign page on upmc.com uses the same line.

evidence.title: UPMC Unleashes New $16M Ad Campaign
evidence.quote: full-page ads in newspapers and magazines, TV ads, a modified logo

evidence.title: Life Changing Is | UPMC
evidence.quote: Because when it changes real lives and whole communities for the better, that's when we call it Life Changing Medicine.

facts.text: PR Daily reported on March 5, 2026 that UPMC runs a patient-creator program, built about three years earlier, in which a typical partnership includes a post on the creator's channel with a collaboration tag, rights for UPMC to reuse the content (including on YouTube Shorts and TikTok) and two weeks of paid amplification, mostly on Meta platforms; some posts drew as many as 200 shares.

evidence.title: Inside a healthcare influencer strategy built on patient voices
evidence.quote: So we built it from nothing and really began thinking about how to leverage real peoples' experiences.

strengths.text: An owned content hub with a published editorial policy (written by staff writers, reviewed by clinicians) and its own email and text sign-ups, so UPMC can reach readers without relying on a social platform.
The MyUPMC portal and app put scheduling, virtual visits, results and billing in one place, and the 2020 figures show the service absorbing a very large jump in video visits.
One brand line in use since 2010 gives campaigns a consistent frame, and the patient-creator program supplies first-person stories that can be reused in short-form video.
The podcast line-up covers different audiences, from general health topics to a show for mental health professionals and a regional series.

gaps.text: The UPMC HealthBeat Podcast looked inactive on its Apple Podcasts listing: the most recent episode shown on 2026-11-10 was dated 06/23/2024.

UPMC is absent from Becker's June 2026 top-five follower lists on all five platforms audited; its own follower counts could not be read for this snapshot because the platform pages block automated fetching.
No current audience figures for HealthBeat or MyUPMC were found on the UPMC pages opened for this snapshot; the newest usage figures found date from June 2020.
